activity_context.topic_title: Limits and Continuity of Multivariable Functions

feedback.worked_solution:
Let the function $f(x,y)$ be defined as

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{2{x}^{2}+x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2xy}.
$$

The function $f(x,y)$ is continuous except when the denominator is zero. However, the point $(-2,3)$ does not cause the denominator to vanish, so we can calculate the limit by substituting  $(-2,3)$ into the function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-2,3)}\frac{2{x}^{2}+x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2xy} & =\frac{2\cdot (-2)^{2}+(-2)\cdot {3}^{2}}{(-2)^{2}+2\cdot (-2)\cdot (3)} \\  & =\frac{8-18}{4-12} \\  & =\frac{-10}{-8} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
